content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem, framing the symptom as account pages failing for shoppers, then building the causal chain starting with failed account page requests and tracing into why those requests triggered the underlying error.

The root cause traces to a monthly-spend-feature flag being switched on starting 15:07, which activated the faulty code path; I'm ruling out deploys since none occurred, confirming the flag change is the only recorded event, and noting the pre-existing ClientDisconnected errors are unrelated baseline noise. I can't pin down exactly what value hit zero in the division error since the stack trace doesn't reveal it, so the evidence trail ends there.

Root cause: with the flag on, account page requests hit a division at spend_summary.py:47 with a zero denominator, raising ZeroDivisionError and failing some requests — the record doesn't explain why the denominator was zero, so I shouldn't speculate. The rollout looks per-evaluation (134/200 on at the switch minute, then all 200), and the error rate peaking at 36% confirms only some requests hit the zero-denominator case, not all of them.

Contributing factors: no test coverage existed for the zero-denominator case in spend_summary.py before the flag went live, so an action item is to add that test. Also the flag flipped from off to fully-on within a minute with no staged rollout, so another action item is requiring gradual rollouts with automatic rollback on error spikes. The underlying code issue — dividing without guarding against zero — is really the root cause itself, so the direct fix is just patching spend_summary.py:47.

What went well: Argus reverted the flag right after the alert fired, and the investigator correctly traced the incident onset to that flag change. What went wrong is murkier — the incident was marked resolved by a person before anyone could confirm the revert actually fixed things, so whether the fix worked is technically unverified rather than a clear process failure.

Got lucky seems unclear, leaving it empty. I'm noting the assumption that the ZeroDivisionError is tied to the flag only by timing correlation, not a direct causal row, and that the revert's effect on errors was never actually verified before closure. For action items, I'm drafting: fix the zero-denominator bug in spend_summary.py before re-enabling the flag, add a test covering that zero-denominator case, and require staged rollout with automatic stop-on-error-rate-rise for io-shop flags.

A fourth action item about confirming error rates returned to baseline after the flag was turned off gets dropped since it's just checking a report, not a real action. I'm working through how to cite timestamps using placeholders in the step text, and reviewing what rules out an earlier deploy or other flag changes as the cause — no deploy occurred the day before onset, and only one other flag change showed up in the hour before, attributed to Argus.

For step 1, I'm citing the account page error spike to 36% at 15:10 alongside the relevant group evidence. Importantly, since the division-by-zero bug at spend_summary.py:47 is still unpatched, flipping the monthly-spend feature flag back on would immediately break account pages again.

action_items.item: Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so a zero divisor is handled and does not fail the request. Do this before monthly-spend-feature is switched on again.
Add a test that runs the spend summary with a zero divisor.
Turn on io-shop feature flags in stages, starting with a small share of traffic.
Make a flag rollout on io-shop stop and switch back off automatically when the account page error rate rises above its baseline.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of account page requests that failed rose from {series_before} before the onset to {series_while_broken} on average, and peaked at {series_at_worst}.
From {began}, account page requests failed with ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: none came back for the day before the onset.
Another flag change: the flag provider showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before, and that was this one.
The ClientDisconnected failures on account pages: they were already present before the onset, while account pages rendered normally and the error rate stayed low.

causal_chain.step: At {P1.1}, admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature. In that same minute, flag evaluations went from all off to mostly on, and after that minute they were all on. The division errors began in the same minute. Before then the flag evaluated off, and account pages rendered normally.

With the flag on, some account page requests ran the spend summary code, and its division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 hit a zero divisor. The record does not show why the divisor was zero for those requests.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a new feature for the shop's account pages, and the code behind it tried to divide by zero for some shoppers, which made their account pages fail.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that exercised the spend summary code behind monthly-spend-feature with a zero divisor before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before any shopper reached it, and the flag would not have been switched on with it in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Flag evaluations went from all off to all on within about a minute. No staged rollout was seen, and nothing was seen that would stop the rollout on a rise in errors.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of account page requests would have run the faulty path, and the rise in errors could have stopped the rollout before most shoppers were affected.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Investigator Agent put the start of the incident at the minute the flag was switched on, and offered the flag change as its leading candidate {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus switched monthly-spend-feature back off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised. The revert can be put back.

input.root_cause: Once monthly-spend-feature was on, some account page requests reached a division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 where the divisor was zero. The ZeroDivisionError this raised failed the whole request. The record does not show why the divisor was zero for those requests.
input.still_at_risk: The division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 is still in the code, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would make account pages fail again.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
